question.problem: Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${10}^{x+1}={3}^{x+2}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x+1} & ={3}^{x+2} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{x+2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1=\operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{x+2})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =(x+2)\operatorname{log}⁡(3) \\ x+1 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{log}⁡(3) \\ x-x\operatorname{log}⁡(3) & =2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)-1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{log}⁡(3)) & =2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)-1 \\ x & =\frac{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)-1}{1-\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$
